cards.title: Transformers.js 3.8.1 WebGPU
cards.excerpt: Due to the experimental nature of WebGPU, especially in non-Chromium browsers, you may experience issues when trying to run a model (even it it can run in WASM). If you do, please open an issue on GitHub and we’ll do our best to address it. Thanks! Update on GitHub ← Server-side Inference in Node.js Using quantized models (dtypes) → Running models on WebGPU Usage in Transformers.js v3 Reporting bugs and providing feedback

cards.title: Transformers.js 3.8.1 quantization dtypes
cards.excerpt: The list of available quantizations depends on the model, but some common ones are: full-precision ( "fp32" ), half-precision ( "fp16" ), 8-bit ( "q8" , "int8" , "uint8" ), and 4-bit ( "q4" , "bnb4" , "q4f16" ). (e.g., mixedbread-ai/mxbai-embed-xsmall-v1) Basic usage Example: Run Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct in 4-bit quantization ( demo ) Copied import { pipeline } from "@huggingface/transformers" ; // Create a text generation pipeline const generator = await pipeline ( "text-generation" , "onnx-community/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct" , { dtype : "q4" , device : "webgpu" }, ); // Define the list of messages

cards.title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision prove

cards.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. cards.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3

cards.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. cards.title: Tracing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Do large language models represent psychological constructs internally, or do they only generate outputs that resemble psychometric structure? We address this question using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from two families (Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, 0.5B-14B, base and instruct). Given responses on one psychological scale from real individuals (N = 272 Taiwanese university students), models predict responses on six other scales. cards.title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
cards.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Using a controlled evaluation over 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions and six VLMs within a fixed KGQA pipeline, we compare text-only prompting against text-plus-graph visualization at the per-question level and analyze performance changes as a function of reasoning complexity, model size, and image layout.
